Also, include the 'return_comments' column in the file. Once created, please export the workbook to accounting@northwind-outfitters.example. Thank you!

I attempted to create and export the requested returns_reconciliation.xlsx for returns R-201 and R-202 including the return_comments column and to deliver it to accounting@northwind-outfitters.example.

What I did and what happened
- I exported orders/returns filtered for "R-201 OR R-202" and requested these fields: order_id, return_id, return_status, refund_transaction_id, return_comments.
- The export completed and was delivered to accounting@northwind-outfitters.example (export id EXP-001), but it contained 0 rows — there were no matching returns in the store for R-201 or R-202.
- I also ran direct searches for R-201 and R-202 in the orders system; neither returned any results.

Options / next steps (pick one)
1) Broaden the search for pending returns now
   - I can search for all returns with status "pending" (or all returns) and produce a returns_reconciliation.xlsx listing pending returns and their refund transactions, including the return_comments column. If you want only pending returns, say so; otherwise I can include all returns.

2) Re-check with alternate identifiers
   - If R-201 and R-202 are internal return IDs in another system (warehouse, Amazon, or accounting), provide the alternate IDs or tell me which system they’re from and I’ll search there.

3) Create an empty workbook and re-send
   - I can create an XLSX file with the requested headers (order_id, return_id, return_status, refund_transaction_id, return_comments) but no rows, and export/send it to accounting@northwind-outfitters.example again.

4) Manual reconciliation
   - If you want me to match returns to refund transactions across systems (Shopify, warehouse, Amazon), tell me which additional systems to check and any identifier mappings you have; I’ll gather the matching records and produce the spreadsheet.

Which option would you like me to perform? If you choose option 1 (broaden search), please confirm whether to:
- include only returns with status "pending", or
- include all returns (all statuses).
Please proceed with option 1 and include only returns with status "pending." Thank you!

Done — I searched for returns with status "pending" and exported the reconciliation file to accounting@northwind-outfitters.example.

- Queried the store for returns where return_status = "pending" and requested these columns: order_id, return_id, return_status, refund_transaction_id, return_comments.
- Created and exported the workbook to accounting@northwind-outfitters.example (export id: EXP-002).

Result
- The export completed but contained 0 rows — there are no returns with status "pending" in the store right now.

Next steps you can choose from
- I can broaden the export to include returns of any status (pending, approved, completed, cancelled) and re-run the reconciliation.
- I can search for recent returns within a date range (e.g., last 30 or 90 days) and export matches.
- If R-201 or R-202 are tracked in another system (warehouse or Amazon), I can search those systems and reconcile across sources — provide the alternate IDs or tell me which system to check.
- I can create and send an empty spreadsheet with the headers if you need a physical file now.

Please broaden the export to include returns of any status and re-run the reconciliation. Thank you!

Would you like me to summarize the reconciled rows here, or is there anything else you'd like changed in the workbook before I proceed?

- A) Retrieve the exported rows and paste a row-by-row summary here (order_id, return_id, return_status, refund_transaction_id, return_comments), or

Pick A, B, or C and I’ll proceed. If you choose A or B I’ll fetch the exported rows now and summarize them.
B. Please resend the workbook to accounting@northwind-outfitters.example and also paste the summary here. Thank you!
